Oil UI
FREE SOURCE / 0.18.0Instruction

From a brief to a page you can inspect.

Give the agent enough context to make a design decision, then ask it to show and verify the result.

01

Install and identify the edition.

Download the ZIP from Finch, extract it and install the oil-ui directory through your agent’s supported Skill mechanism. Ask the agent to read SKILL.md. These instructions target source 0.18.0; if Oil UI Pro is installed, its overlapping workflow takes precedence.

02

Share a brief that can guide decisions.

State the audience, first-screen task, real content, device constraints and deliverable. Add the project, a screenshot or existing brand assets. Say whether you want a review, a mockup or runnable interface files.

03

Choose a direction, then a layout.

For a new interface, version 0.18.0 normally begins with 4–6 style cards. Select a style, then compare 2–3 layout alternatives before expanding a page. An existing confirmed direction can be refined directly.

Compare directions using the same brief

Keep the headline, dates, and booking action fixed so the visual treatment is the part you compare.

04

Build and inspect the actual result.

Run the representative interface in the target environment. Inspect screenshots at the sizes people will use. Check readability, clipping and the primary action separately from design quality.

Test the primary action and combined filters

Follow the booking button to its destination and check that mobile filters combine correctly.

05

Keep the result and its limits together.

Deliver the editable output, chosen direction, screenshots, changes made and unresolved issues. A working interface requires project-specific implementation and interaction checks; a screenshot alone does not prove those behaviors.

Capture a reproducible review state

Record the active filter, sort column, and selected incident alongside the screenshot.

Prompts to adapt

Explore a new direction

Use Oil UI to design a pottery-class booking page for first-time visitors. Keep the class price, materials and session details consistent across four style cards. We need a clear next step and a layout that works on phones.

Review an existing interface

Review this account-settings screen at desktop and mobile sizes. Focus on visual hierarchy, readability and the save action. Give evidence and prioritized recommendations; do not change the code yet.

Refine an agreed direction

Keep the selected coastal-glaze style. Refine the typography and spacing of the class detail panel, preserve the content and primary action, then show the before and after screenshots.

Use the tools included in this edition.

Run commands from the extracted oil-ui directory. The configuration describes the same content and 4–6 distinct card styles. See the bundled example and reference documents for the complete schema.

python3 scripts/build_style_cards.py cards.json --out ./directions
python3 scripts/build_explorer.py manifest.json --output ./comparison.html

Optional screenshot capture of your own page:

node scripts/shoot.mjs ./page.html --size 390x844,1280x900 --full --out ./shots

The comparison artifact may use JavaScript and sandboxed previews. These Finch presentation documents contain neither scripts nor embedded frames.

Know what you are looking at.

Without image viewing, the agent can produce code or design notes but cannot verify visual quality. Without a runnable project, it cannot confirm end-to-end interaction behavior. Network and optional provider access are separate dependencies.
